note: Ground truth, written by reading step.html and step-mega.js — NOT by running
the tool and blessing what it found. That distinction is the whole value of
this file: a corpus built from the tool's own output can only ever score 100%.
Several components are BUILT BY JAVASCRIPT after load (mega-nav's items, the
hero slides, the deal tabs, the FAQ accordion, the branch-locator detail).
Their selectors are taken from the template literals in step-mega.js, so the
labels describe the page as a user meets it rather than as it is served.
`hidden: true` marks a component that exists only while opened. The survey
cannot see it, and a scorer that counts it as a miss is measuring the wrong
thing — it is scored separately, under `openable`.
`type: "none"` pins something that must NOT be flagged — a near-miss built
into the page on purpose (a lone button whose class says 'modal', a layout
table, a price slider). Never scored for recall; a detection matching one is
a CONFIRMED false positive.
Tab strips are labelled `tabs`. Until stage 4 restores the tabs/menu split,
both harnesses accept `menu` for them and print the count owed.
`single: true` on an accordion marks a lone disclosure — one trigger, one
panel. The type stays accordion by decision; the flag is for stage 4.

components.why: Seven top-level triggers, each opening a panel of links. One menu, not seven. Rooted on ul.mega-nav__list (id megaNav), NOT on the .mega-nav <nav> that wraps it: u1.fix.menu reads the root's OWN CHILDREN, and the nav has exactly one child — this list. Rooted on the wrapper it is a menu of one item. That is the engine's contract, not a preference, so the wrapper was simply the wrong label.

Five sibling controls over five panels that swap in place — the textbook tab strip. Was relabelled `menu` when the collapse was decided; restored to `tabs` for the stage-4 split. Harnesses accept `menu` for it meanwhile, counted and warned.
Six sibling controls over ONE re-rendered region. A strip over one region is still the shape, and the already-selected one belongs to it. Restored to `tabs`, menu accepted until stage 4.
The same strip shape again, over the accordion below it. Restored to `tabs`, menu accepted until stage 4.

The FAQ items under the tab strip: several sibling header buttons, each opening its answer in place. Built by mega.js — invisible to the jsdom harness until its renderer list included faqTabs/faq, and reported as a false positive for exactly that reason. It was a real accordion all along; the corpus was short.
aria-roledescription=carousel, prev/next, dots, and a 6.5s auto-advance.
Five of them, one per finder panel. A selector that matches all five is correct here.

A real <form>: five labelled fields, a required consent checkbox, a submit button. Flagged by the tool and unlabelled until the precision metric surfaced it — the finding was about the corpus, not the detector.
The membership-tiers comparison. Was rooted on bare `.data-table`, which matches whichever of the page's four data tables happens to come first — each table now carries its own id and its own label.
The size conversion chart — a real <table> with scope'd headers and a caption.
The four-flagship spec comparison — a real <table>.
The branch detail pane renders an opening-hours <table> per selected store. Rooted on the pane because the table inside is rebuilt on every selection.

The branch list: sibling buttons with aria-current, pressing one re-renders the fixed detail pane beside it — behaviourally identical to dealTabs (panel swapped in one place = tabs). Unlabelled until 4.3's swap-in-place rule started seeing it; the detection was right, the corpus was short (corpus change, not code).
role=dialog aria-modal=true, opened from the Search button.
A drawer is a modal by behaviour: it covers the page and traps focus.
The size-guide modal, opened from two [data-modal-open] buttons. Flagged by the tool and unlabelled until the precision metric surfaced it.

A trail: links with a separator between each pair, in text smaller than the body. Labelled `menu` until the rule was decided — it is navigation, but it is not a menu, and it now has a type of its own.
My account: a button opening a list of five real links, OUTSIDE any <nav>. A dropdown of links is a menu wherever it lives — the footer demotion and the nav requirement must not eat it.
A Bootstrap-style dropdown: data-toggle=dropdown, no aria-controls, real hrefs inside. The commonest dropdown dialect on the web; deliberately edge-poor so only class or behaviour can find it.

A replaced <select>: hidden native control, visible toggle whose TEXT CHANGES to the chosen option, options that select a value rather than navigate. The Molina pattern, pinned. Items are buttons, not links — a listbox, not a menu.

An autocomplete: the suggestion list is EMPTY until typing fills it — the commonest autocomplete shape, and the one the count-based probe rung exists for. role=combobox on the input in the friendly build only; hostile must name it from the typing.

The live-chat panel: fixed, floating over the page, opened by the FAB. A real openable component the corpus simply had no label for — it was counted as a false positive in every build until this entry (owner decision, 4.2 era: corpus change, not code).
A 420px fixed confirm box with a backdrop and NO role anywhere — the small dialog the overlay size test cannot see. Declared via data-panel-target on its trigger.
A single disclosure: one trigger with aria-expanded, one adjacent panel of prose. Type accordion by decision, with single:true for the stage-4 subtype.
role=tooltip, hidden until its control is described. The role was never in COMPONENT_BY_ROLE, so it rode in on the edges and then had no name.

7.1: an <a href="#"> whose click flips its own state (class + text) and never navigates — a button in link's clothing. The behavioural voice carries it: pressed, changed, navigated:false, nothing revealed. The dead-href markup arm was deliberately narrowed — this very page has 31 innocent href="#" links.
7.1: a bare div with tabindex=0 and a pointer cursor whose click flips its own state — a button with no role at all. tabindex on a non-control is also the markup arm's hint.
7.1's negative: a REAL link (href=/sale) styled with the same btn classes as its neighbours. Styling must not make a working link a button — and a healthy link is not a component to publish.

7.2 (owner spec): role=switch IS a component — checkbox, subtype switch, state in aria-checked. Relabelled from the earlier pinned negative, whose real point survives: the class says switch-nav and 'nav' must still never make it a menu.

7.2: a radio with no role anywhere — three styled sibling divs, choosing one marks it (data-checked + class) and unmarks the previous choice. The mutual exclusion is the tell; root is the common parent.

7.9: a spinner that appears on the press and hides itself 600ms later, under 20 characters of text the whole time. u1.fix.loading needs exactly one part — loadingBar, announced when it appears — so the transient element itself is the root. Behavioural: appeared, then vanished with nobody un-pressing.

7.9: the page-level skeleton — a shimmer block whose content never arrives, sitting visibly on the page. The MARKUP arm's pin (class carries the word); the self-swapping variant is exercised in the unit tests, where the idle window is controlled — a walk that reaches a section after its skeleton swapped has nothing left to see, and that is the honest limit.
7.9's negative: role=progressbar WITH aria-valuenow — a progress meter reporting a value, not a loading announcement. u1.fix.loading must not be proposed for it.
7.8: a pager with an ELLIPSIS — 1 … 4 5 6 … 12 plus prev/next. The nav says pagination in its aria-label (markup arm); the run of numbers with gaps must satisfy the counting arm too.
7.8: load-more — a button whose press ADDS three siblings to the list above it. Pagination, subtype load-more; the growth is the tell, no page numbers anywhere.
7.7: a table people OPERATE — a Rebook button in a third of its cells. u1.fix.grid manages arrow-key cell navigation a data table never needs; control density is the tell, no role anywhere.
7.7: the responsive div-table — display:table markup, three agreeing rows of two cells, no <table> element in sight. Table by shape, marked maybe.

7.6: a WIZARD — one form walked through in steps: two sibling panels of fields, exactly one showing, next/back between them. formShape reads kind:wizard; #wizNoName inside is the deliberately nameless field the unlabeled-fields finding must list.

7.6's negative: an input+button pair whose button only COPIES — the search-form shape without a submit. A row that submits nothing is not a FORM to map. `allow: button` because on the hostile build the copy control is a bare div, and calling THAT a button is the 7.1 rule doing its job.

7.5: the PORTAL combobox — the suggestion list lives at the end of <body>, the way floating-ui/portal libraries render it, and only aria-owns names the connection. The typing pass must find the far list; comboboxShape must accept it.
7.5's negative, formalised: a page FILTER — typing narrows a list that was always visible. probeTyping tells it from a combobox by when the list existed; pinned so the distinction never regresses.

7.4: a popup month — weekday row, thirty running day buttons, a month-and-year header — opened from the calendar button beside a date field. The counting alone is NOT enough (see the locker grid); the weekday row or the month name is the necessary second witness.
7.4's negative: thirty-two RUNNING NUMBERS in a grid — a locker picker. Counting alone must never say calendar; there is no weekday row and no month name here, on purpose.
7.3: vertical tabs — three stacked sibling buttons swapping panels beside them. Orientation must not matter to the strip rule; rooted on the list per the direct-parent contract.
7.3: hash-tabs — anchors whose href is the #id of a sibling panel, exactly one showing. Tabs by MARKUP alone (the hint arm), and by behaviour when pressed.
7.3's negative: in-page links to VISIBLE page sections — a table of contents. The hash-tabs rule must not fire when the targets are far, visible, and not each other's siblings.
7.2's negative: label > input[type=checkbox][hidden] + span — the native checkbox under styling. The browser already runs it; mapping it would announce it twice.
A lone button whose CLASS says menu-toggle, outside any nav, opening nothing on this page. A part-name is not a component.
A lone button whose CLASS says open-modal. The class rule that reads 'modal' must not call the BUTTON a dialog.
A price range control — input[type=range] in a wrapper whose class says slider. A slider is not a carousel.
A static image grid whose class says gallery. Nothing cycles, nothing hides — not a carousel.

A 3×3 <table role="presentation"> used for layout. The role is the author saying 'not a table'; detection must listen. `allow: table` — the REALISTIC build strips role=presentation, and a 3-row headerless grid of values is then structurally identical to a price list; maybe-table there is a defensible reading, not the FP this pin exists for.
Three selects and a type=button 'Clear'. Fields plus a clickable is not a form — nothing here submits anywhere.
A div whose class says tabs-content, sitting inside a strip. The CONTENT of tabs is not the tabs.
The mini strip AROUND the tabs-content decoy is itself a real two-tab strip — two sibling buttons swapping panels in place. The decoy pins what must not be flagged; this pins what must.

note: The four `.rail` strips are horizontal scrollers with prev/next buttons,
and `.ticker` is an auto-advancing marquee. Whether each is 'a carousel' is
a judgement call a specialist makes, so they are held apart from the scored
set rather than counted as a hit or a false positive either way.
